subject: Lab checklist: InferAPI vs hyperscaler — latency & throughput probe
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@hyperwave.ai>, Priya Shah <pshah@hyperwave.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lab checklist: InferAPI vs hyperscaler — latency & throughput probe

Thanks again for the call this morning — good signals on product fit and the ops questions. Per our conversation, below is a concise checklist so we can align on the competitive probe scope and owners before we run the A/B sweep. I kept it narrow so we can get meaningful p95/p99 and tokens/sec numbers in the next 7 business days.

Quick recap of ask from HyperWave: they want a head-to-head for a representative customer workload (chat + short context retrieval) to validate p95/p99 and sustained tokens/sec under a capped latency SLO. They emphasized cold-starts and multi-tenant noise.

Planned scope (proposed):
- Workloads: 1) Chat (prompt length ~120 tokens, response ~150 tokens) 2) Retrieval-augmented single-turn (prompt 80 tokens + 512 token context).
- Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec (sustained), tail variance, failure/retry rate under 95th percentile load.
- A/B pairs: Redwood-BaseQ4 (quantized) vs HyperCloud-XL (their managed endpoint); Redwood-BaseQ4 with caching enabled vs without.
- Environment: US-west region, identical concurrency targets (60 concurrent sessions), warm cache priming, 30-minute warmup window.

Owners & immediate asks:
- Jonas: capture the exact request/response harness and run the first smoke test (today). Please attach the ab-test-config.yaml to the Drive folder.
- Karthik: prepare kernel/quant settings we should lock for parity and list any hardware differences we need to call out in the readout.
- Marcus: run a short p95/p99 micro-sweep for the chat profile and paste results (csv) to the shared folder.
- Samir/Priya: confirm the HyperWave endpoint URL + any concurrency limits and whether they will pin a single model version for the test.

Deliverables (timeline):
- Smoke run + harness check (Jonas) — EOD 2025-06-18
- First A/B sweep (30m steady-state per configuration) — 2025-06-19 morning
- Raw CSV plus short readout (Marcus) — 2025-06-19 afternoon
- Joint readout call — propose 2025-06-20 10:00 PT (please confirm)

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (call recording) + initial template (ab-test-config.yaml).

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (video/mp4)
Attachment: ab-test-config.yaml (text/yaml)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@hyperwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lab checklist: InferAPI vs hyperscaler — latency & throughput probe

Thanks Naomi — I started the harness and pushed a minimal config to the Drive folder (ab-test-config.yaml). Key notes from the smoke:
- Default Redwood-BaseQ4 quant path yields ~850 tokens/sec sustained on our g4dn-like test node when warmed.
- p95/p99 (chat profile) after 15m warmup: p95=42ms, p99=120ms (see attached csv draft).
- Observed spike behavior: when we increased concurrency from 60->90 the p99 blows out because of KV-cache thrashing; will add a cache pin config for the A run.

Open questions for HyperWave to confirm for parity:
1) Will you pin a single model revision for the run?
2) Can you guarantee a warm cache / pinned instance for the 30-minute steady window?
3) Any rate limiting or per-tenant throttles we should configure on our side?

I'll run the formal 30-minute A/B sweep tomorrow morning if we have answers to the above. Dropping the draft CSV: latency-p95-p99-results.csv into Drive.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: latency-p95-p99-results.csv (text/csv)

From: Samir Patel <samir@hyperwave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@hyperwave.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 14:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lab checklist: InferAPI vs hyperscaler — latency & throughput probe

Appreciate the checklist — quick answers:
- We will pin HyperCloud-XL rev b3 for the window and can provide a warmed-up instance.
- Endpoint: https://api.hypercloud.ai/v1/models/hypercloud-xl/rev-b3 (no auth token required for the test harness IPs we shared).
- Concurrency limits: we can accept the 60 concurrent sessions test; beyond that we throttle to protect other tenants — so stay at 60.

A couple of requests from our side to keep apples-to-apples:
- Please include cold-start samples (single request after idle 30m) in a separate run and label them in the CSV. Our multi-tenant noise shows up there.
- Can Redwood provide a run with and without prefix caching so we can see delta?

We'll be on standby tomorrow morning. 10:00 PT on 2025-06-20 works for a readout.

Samir
Samir Patel
Principal SRE, HyperWave Systems
samir@hyperwave.ai
Attachment: none

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@hyperwave.ai>, Priya Shah <pshah@hyperwave.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lab checklist: InferAPI vs hyperscaler — latency & throughput probe

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmations and for pinning rev b3. Updated plan based on Samir's notes:
- We'll run:
  1) Warmed A/B sweep (30m steady-state per config) at 60 concurrency
  2) Cold-start batch (single request after 30m idle) labeled separately
  3) Repeat A/B with prefix cache disabled to measure delta

Action items and owners:
- Jonas: execute the warmed A/B and cold-start runs (2025-06-19 morning) — upload CSVs to Drive when each completes.
- Marcus: produce the short readout (1 page) with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and a small table for cold vs warm results (2025-06-19 EOD).
- Karthik: prepare a short appendix listing config differences we should call out in the external readout (hardware SKU, quant flags) — 2025-06-19 EOD.
- Naomi: schedule the joint readout on 2025-06-20 10:00 PT and prepare a 10-min slide with topline deltas and a recommended next test.

If anything slips, flag it here and we'll push the readout by 24 hours. Thanks all — looking forward to a crisp dataset.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: none
